inputs.original_text: Powerful governments are driving this crisis, while civilians with the least ability to flee or recover are made to bear the cost. Threats to civilian areas and essential infrastructure put people’s access to vital services at risk; that is not an acceptable side effect of political decisions. Claims of a “just war” mean little without accountability and meaningful protection for civilians. We should reject the idea that wider regional war is inevitable and demand de-escalation and protection for those most at risk.
inputs.modified_text: This crisis is being driven by powerful governments, but civilians—especially those with the fewest ways to escape or recover—are paying the price. When civilian areas and essential infrastructure are threatened, access to vital services is put at risk; that cannot be brushed off as an unavoidable side effect of political choices. Talk of a “just war” is empty without accountability and real protection for civilians. Wider regional war is not inevitable: de-escalation and the safety of those most at risk must come first.
